item.title: Definition of Cancellation Laws
item.description: Let D be an integral domain with a,b,c\in D. If a\ne0, then ab=ac\implies b=c. Similarly, ba=ca\implies b=c.

item.title: Definition of an Integral Domain
item.description: If we have a commutative ring with unity R, then R is an integral domain if it has no zero divisors (e.g. \mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Q}, \mathbb{R}, and \mathbb{C}): Commutative, Unity is 1, a \cdot b=0\iff a=0\text{ or }b=0.

item.title: Definition of a Zero Divisor
item.description: Let R be a commutative ring. We say that an element r\in R is a zero divisor if a \cdot b=0 for some element b\ne0 of R.
